claims.text: As-fabricated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of 786 MPa.
As-fabricated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
As-fabricated HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal strain of 13.5%.
As-fabricated HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility.
HfZrTiTa0.53 should be subjected to a short-duration sub-transus anneal followed by rapid quenching.
The proposed heat treatment will create a dual-phase microstructure.
The proposed heat treatment will refine the grain structure.
The proposed heat treatment will produce enriched, ductile grain-boundary regions.
Sub-transus annealing will induce partial recrystallization in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Sub-transus annealing will induce controlled phase separation at grain boundaries.
The resulting microstructure will alter local dislocation mobility and promote more uniform plastic flow.
More uniform plastic flow will delay necking and localized tensile failure.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater tensile uniform elongation than the as-fabricated control.
The heat-treated alloy's tensile uniform elongation will exceed the reported 13.5% terminal strain.
The heat treatment will preserve yield strength at approximately 786 MPa without a significant decrease.
The heat treatment will preserve compressive strength at approximately 1314 MPa without a significant decrease.
The heat treatment will retain high impact-triggered energy release.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has baseline impact-test energy release comparable to tungsten-alloy comparisons.
The hypothesis is limited to room-temperature, quasi-static tensile and compression loading near 10^-3 s^-1 and comparable thin-steel-target impact conditions.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is identified as terminal strain but is then used as a quantitative benchmark for tensile uniform elongation; these are distinct mechanical quantities and are not established as directly comparable.
